change: Validate native selection/store identity and current lease before committing initial owner registration, so a refused admission cannot strand a new binding.
red_behavior: The original helper committed an SQLite binding row, then refused the changed policy: observed 1 row where rollback required 0.
invariants: Native StateLock stays held across absence validation, callback and SQL commit. Final native check reads selected policy and original store identity without acquiring another StateLock or reentering the workflow mutex.
Production caller invokes the supplied final native check inside the workflow transaction, after registration writes and before commit; it also checks the guard and current SQL lease/binding.
Failure rolls back new owner, binding and event rows with the original transaction. No compensating deletion or removal of an existing binding is used.

The native helper no longer performs a fallible post-commit check that could misreport a committed registration as a rolled-back refusal. Returned binding is descriptive and later dispatch gates remain mandatory.
Destination audit validation occurs before SQL; its lock is not acquired inside the SQL writer.
limits: This fixes a registration leak in the pending integration, not proof of the cause of the eight existing retained production sessions. Those sessions are unchanged.

Core regression uses a real private policy/store fixture and a real SQLite registration transaction; workflow tests cover the actual registration tables with descriptive native-binding fixtures. No production VM/provider call, complete source/resource admission or shipping acceptance is claimed.
The older metadata-only registration API remains for existing callers/fixtures; production native registration uses the checked transaction API.

Normal owner consumer, complete C/R/productive transition, preserved gate exits, capacity recovery, independent approval, normal rollout and all original live CLI/Discord/shipping/fault/soak requirements remain incomplete.
